Attainment and Attendance in Adur

What the national model behind How to Pull the Right Lever says about the district’s secondary schools, within West Sussex and alongside Brighton and Hove. Draft for discussion.

Author
Affiliation

Adam Dennett

Bartlett Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis, University College London

Published

October 31, 2026

WarningDraft for discussion

One of the district documents for Sussex. It sits beneath the West Sussex document, and the district summary compares all of the districts. Every figure comes from published Department for Education data and the national models of How to Pull the Right Lever. Nothing uses pupil-level records. The commentary is written to a common pattern from the figures; read it as a starting point for discussion.

Summary

Adur’s results are above the middle of England’s districts, on an intake less disadvantaged than England’s. Its 2 state secondary schools are in Shoreham-by-Sea and Sompting.

  • Overall results: 48.4 in Attainment 8 in 2024/25, 80th of 265 districts in England.
  • Disadvantage: 19.9% of pupils are disadvantaged, against 28.3% nationally.
  • Disadvantaged pupils average 40.0, above the national 37.8 (72nd of 265).
  • The gap between disadvantaged pupils and the rest is 10.6 points, the 194th widest of 265.

The other findings:

  • For all pupils, Adur is 1.4 points above England. The largest pieces in the national model are Ofsted ratings (+1.0) and West Sussex’s county-wide effect (-0.7). The district’s schools add 1.4 points beyond what the model expects.
  • For disadvantaged pupils it is 0.9 points above England. The largest pieces are West Sussex’s county-wide effect (-1.5) and being in the South East (-1.3), and the schools add 4.1 points beyond what the model expects.
  • No district effect can be found. Once intake, West Sussex’s county effect and the schools themselves are accounted for, nothing is left that all Adur schools share.
  • 1 of the 2 schools is above expectation over 2021/22 to 2024/25. The strongest is Shoreham Academy (+3.5); the weakest The Sir Robert Woodard Academy (-0.6).
  • Absence was 7.8% in autumn and spring 2025/26 (7.9% a year earlier), against 8.0% for England and 8.1% for West Sussex. Over 2021/22 to 2024/25 its schools ran 0.3 points below what their intakes predict.
  • Reduced timetables run at 1.3 times the national rate, and suspensions at 0.4 times (7.6 per 100 pupils, against 21.2).
  • Disadvantaged groups are small, 43 to 59 pupils a year per school. Every school-level figure for them moves from year to year and should be read over several years.

1 About this analysis

Adur is a district of West Sussex, not a local authority, and that shapes what can be said:

  • The national models place schools in local authorities. The “local authority effect” in this document is West Sussex’s, shared with every school in the county.
  • What is particular to Adur shows up in its schools’ own residuals, and in the district test of Section 6.
  • Absence and exclusions are summed over the district’s 2 schools, followed through any change of URN.
  • Ranks. With 2 schools, Adur is placed among the 264 districts in England with five or more schools. A district this small moves a long way with one school’s results.

The methods are described in full in the East Sussex document.

4 What explains attainment in Adur

The decomposition for Adur, in Attainment 8 points. ‘Place’ is West Sussex’s effect plus the South East’s; ‘unexplained’ is what the district’s own schools add beyond everything the model accounts for.
Factor All pupils Disadvantaged Non-disadvantaged

For all pupils, Adur is 1.4 points above England. The pieces of at least a quarter of a point:

  • Ofsted ratings (+0.99);
  • West Sussex’s county-wide effect (-0.74);
  • the teacher workforce (+0.60);
  • being in the South East (-0.46);
  • absence (-0.37);
  • prior attainment (-0.33);
  • the level of disadvantage (+0.26);
  • and the district’s schools themselves (+1.43), beyond what the model expects.

For disadvantaged pupils, Adur is 0.9 points above England. The pieces of at least a quarter of a point:

  • West Sussex’s county-wide effect (-1.47);
  • being in the South East (-1.32);
  • Ofsted ratings (+0.94);
  • English as an additional language (-0.53);
  • absence (-0.39);
  • admissions (-0.30);
  • and the district’s schools themselves (+4.14), beyond what the model expects.

5 The disadvantaged gap, school by school

No Adur school is above expectation for its non-disadvantaged pupils while more than a point below it for its disadvantaged ones. Shoreham Academy is above expectation for both groups. The table below gives each school’s own persistent effect, from the model with a school term, which is the steadier measure.

6 Is there an Adur effect?

The district test of the East Sussex document adds a district level to the national model, with and without each school’s own record.

None of Adur’s district effects can be told apart from zero on either specification. The district’s results are explained by its intake, West Sussex’s county effect and its individual schools.

7 Absence

  • 7.8% absence in autumn and spring 2025/26, against 8.0% for England and 8.1% for West Sussex. A year earlier it was 7.9%.
  • Persistent absence is 22.4%, against 21.6% for England.
  • Against its intake, the district’s schools run 0.25 points below what their pupils’ profiles predict, on average over 2021/22 to 2024/25.
  • No school runs more than a point above its predicted absence.

Reduced timetables account for 0.38% of sessions, against 0.29% in England, 1.3 times the national rate. Shoreham Academy’s rate is the highest in the district.

1 of the 2 schools is above the national average absence in 2024/25. Bringing it to it would add up to 0.7 points for all pupils, as an indication of scale.

Suspensions were 7.6 per 100 pupils in 2024/25, against 21.2 for England and 16.2 for West Sussex.

9 Questions for discussion

  1. Disadvantaged pupils. They average 40.0 in Adur against 37.8 in England, and the district’s schools add 4.1 points for them beyond what the model expects. Both of its schools are above expectation for these pupils; what they do is worth sharing across West Sussex.
  2. Attendance is a modest lever. Absence costs the district 0.4 points against England for all pupils.
  3. Schools, not the place. There is no Adur district effect: the differences that matter are between its schools.
  4. Practice. Reduced timetables and suspensions are close to or below the national rate.
  5. The county. West Sussex’s own effect for disadvantaged pupils is -3.8% (131st of 151), distinguishable from zero, and it applies to every school here. The county questions in the West Sussex document apply here as well.

Notes on method

Methods and sources are those of the East Sussex document. District membership comes from each school’s postcode (ONS postcode directory, via postcodes.io). Absence and exclusions for the district are summed over its schools, including any predecessor or successor URNs. This document is generated from templates/district_report.qmd by R/20_district_reports.R, from data built by R/17_area_analysis.R, R/18_district_effects.R and R/19_trust_effects.R. Its format is described in AREA_REPORTS.md.
